rationale.oversight-explanation: Complete adversarial debate helps humans interpret and judge AI recommendations.
rationale.ai-review: Independent agents challenge, synthesize, and assess candidate evaluations.
rationale.risk-routing: Bias, disagreement, confidence, and data signals trigger priority human review.
rationale.hitl-workflow: Mandatory review, override authority, and interruption controls constrain decisions.
rationale.oversight-theater: Paper critiques nominal review that merely rubber-stamps opaque recommendations.
rationale.regulatory-compliance: Architecture explicitly operationalizes EU AI Act Articles 14, 26, and 27.
rationale.provenance-auditability: Tamper-evident logs preserve inputs, reasoning, reviewer actions, and decisions.
rationale.framework: Reusable reference architecture maps integrated components into a compliance workflow.
rationale.design-only: Buildable architecture is specified without implementation or evaluation evidence.
rationale.general-ai: Oversight targets employment decision AI, not AI-generated software.
rationale.non-developer: Recruiters and organizational reviewers oversee candidate assessments.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Adversarial presentation and engagement tracking explicitly mitigate automation bias.
